narrative_passages.title: Thamud and the she-camel
narrative_passages.treatment_reason: Read only; no one is shown.

summary_for_children: Ash-Shams means The Sun. It swears by the sun, moon, day, night and the soul, and says success is in purifying the soul. It recalls the she-camel of Thamud.
environment_concept: A sundial in a bright square (91:1) and a still round pool beside it, where the moon is seen when it follows the sun (91:2). Further on, an old stone well with an empty drinking trough (91:13) below cliffs with carved doorways, for Thamud (91:11). No person and no she-camel are shown, and the destruction of 91:14 is not pictured.
architecture_and_scenery: Sundial, still reflecting pool, a stone well and trough, sandstone cliffs with carved doorways.

depiction_rules: No prophet, person or representation of Allah is shown. Unseen realities are never pictured. Interactive activities are labelled as adaptations.

unique_world.visual_theme: A whitewashed village hall at sunset with the moon rising after the sun and a great tarnished brass lamp on a stand

primary_mechanic.text: Polish twelve patches of a tarnished brass lamp: steady rubbing clears most; three stubborn patches need ash paste (rubbing alone is refused past a point); paste on ordinary brass is refused as scratching; the lamp brightens and lights the hall when clean (91:9-10, the one who purifies it; the lamp is only a picture).

secondary_activities: Thamud denied (91:11-15, read only; Salih and the she-camel are not shown)
unique_world.narrative_structure: A reading on the lane at sunset, the lamp, then a reading outside the hall
environment_behaviour: the lamp’s brass brightens patch by patch
it lights the hall when fully polished
unique_world.learning_objective: Know that the successful one purifies the soul (91:9-10)

story_library.source: Owner's 'Quran Adventure — Children's Story Library' (2026-11-04), first-draft narration for ages about 7-12
story_library.title: The Sun and the Soul
story_library.children_narration: The Quran draws our attention to the sun, moon, day, night, and the human soul. It teaches that people have a responsibility to cultivate goodness rather than wrongdoing. It also recalls the people of Thamud and the she-camel.

world_idea.title: The Sun and Moon Valley
world_idea.description: Explore shifting daylight and moonlight, then enter a separate Thamud narrative environment.

story_library.checks: Every reference exists in the verified text (checked 2026-11-04). Narration is draft, written by the owner, not reviewed by a scholar.
story_library.rule_conflicts_resolved: The she-camel and its hamstringing (91:13-14): the camel may appear alive in the narrative place; the hamstringing is narration only.
